clocks.label: SAXONY-ANHALT
clocks.why: Germany's Saxony-Anhalt votes with the AfD polling about 41.8 per cent against the CDU's 22.4. This clock prices GEO-028, opened today at 16 per cent: the firewall is a coalition rule and coalition rules are irrelevant against an absolute majority of SEATS. Watch the seat count, not the vote share.

clocks.label: KYIV PAUSE ENDS
clocks.why: Putin's 72-hour instruction that no strikes be carried out on Kyiv runs from midnight Saturday, and Zelenskyy said Ukraine would hold its own fire. This is our new dated falsifier on GEO-005 at 20 per cent, replacing the 14 September envoy window that resolved today on the confirming side: if the pause lapses with no extension and no jointly acknowledged text, GEO-005 comes back to 17.

clocks.label: VENEZUELA TEXT
clocks.why: Caracas said a signing session was scheduled. This clock prices GEO-022, held at 36 per cent: if it passes with no published instrument - no governing law, no arbitration seat, no named sanctions authorisation - a 100-year concession exists only as a briefing. Today's Reuters reporting that a US money-laundering inquiry into the venture's operator was paused says the deal is built around a PERSON rather than around infrastructure.

clocks.label: BOJ DECISION
clocks.why: The Bank of Japan's policy meeting, and the clock behind GEO-025 at 28 per cent. Japan is where the world borrows cheaply; the ten-year JGB is near 3 per cent, the highest since 1996. A hike plus the yen through 150 is the confirmation leg - a rate decision in Tokyo transmitted as a margin call everywhere the cheap yen was spent.

clocks.label: HORMUZ FALSIFIER
clocks.why: Our own dated falsifier, published in advance so it can be scored against us - and deliberately NOT reinterpreted today. It requires an attack on a laden tanker inside the INTERNATIONAL LANES; the reported Kharg strike was at a loading anchorage roughly 250 nautical miles up the Gulf. If no such attack occurs by this date AND Muscat publishes a minesweeping calendar, the recurrence read is a MISS: GEO-001 back toward 21, GEO-003 back to about 38.

clocks.label: XI SUMMIT
clocks.why: The state visit GEO-006 now at 89 per cent and GEO-012 at 31 per cent both hang on, and the date Washington wants its overcapacity finding published before. Reuters reports Xi assembling an unusually large CEO delegation and Notus reports a state dinner in preparation - sunk organisational cost, which is the only evidence a scheduled-visit question should move on. Brent's band question resolves the same day: our first Brier score.

speculation.obs: The imagery record on the site Trump threatened tonight says it was being hardened, not operated. As published by the Institute for Science and International Security from commercial satellite imagery, work at the two Pickaxe Mountain tunnel entrances involved concrete being poured over the western entrance extension and rock and soil pushed back and levelled over an eastern portal, with dump trucks, cement mixers, backhoes and truck-mounted cranes moving through the complex; by late April two eastern entrances had been partly blocked with earthen material that would need heavy equipment to clear. The same analysts assessed that the facility was likely not yet ready for operations, while noting smaller closed-roof vehicles near the entrances consistent with interior outfitting, and were openly doubtful that the visible utility support would be sufficient for enrichment inside the tunnel.
speculation.src: Institute for Science and International Security imagery reports (11 February 2026 report on 10 February imagery; follow-up late April), corroborated by Iran International and Times of Israel coverage of the same imagery
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and it is the piece that makes tonight's threat legible. The observed behaviour - overburden being added, portals being deliberately blocked, no sign of the power and cooling an enrichment hall needs - is consistent with a site being prepared to survive bombing rather than a site producing anything yet. That matters two ways. It weakens the urgency case for striking now, because you cannot destroy centrifuges that are not installed; and it strengthens the case that the threat has coercive rather than military value, which is what a target repeatedly named since mid-July and still unstruck normally indicates. Note honestly that this imagery record is months old and is the public record, not tonight's picture - what the US government sees now is a different dataset, and a change in it is exactly the thing that would not be published in advance.
speculation.falsifier: Fresh commercial imagery showing power lines, substations, cooling plant or spoil consistent with an operating hall would kill the not-yet-operational read and make an urgency case real. An IAEA access arrangement covering Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La would settle it directly. A strike executed on the complex would confirm the target was military rather than rhetorical - and continued repetition of the threat without a strike confirms the opposite.

speculation.obs: The transit series that supported our read has turned against it. As published by Lloyd's List Intelligence from Joint Maritime Information Center data, movements through Bab al-Mandab fell to 202 traceable transits between 24 and 30 August, down from at least 302 (257 of them AIS-traceable) between 17 and 23 August. The weekly average from 27 July to 23 August was 273 ships, and the average before the Saudi naval ban took effect on 20 July was 319. The same brief records a single named incident in the window - a projectile strike on a Bahri-owned VLCC off Yanbu on 24 August - and no attacks reported after that date, while JMIC still assesses that the risk to commercial shipping remains substantial.
speculation.src: Lloyd's List Intelligence Red Sea Brief, 3 September 2026, reporting Joint Maritime Information Center transit data
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and it goes first because it is the number that could embarrass us. We have been arguing this is a DISCRIMINATING blockade - a quarrel with Riyadh priced by underwriters as a threat to a specific subset of Saudi-linked tonnage, not to trade generally - and the strongest evidence for that was a transit count holding up under a ground offensive. A third of the traffic leaving in a single week is the first hard datapoint the other way. The honest alternative readings are that this is the delayed insurance response to the 24 August Yanbu strike rather than to the Mokha fighting, or simple weekly noise in a series that swings by dozens of hulls. One week is not a trend and 202 is still two-thirds of the pre-ban norm, so the read is downgraded rather than abandoned.
speculation.falsifier: A second consecutive week near or below 200 confirms the strait itself is being repriced and the discriminating read is dead. A rebound above the 273-a-week August average restores it. A laden hull with no Saudi charter, owner or cargo link struck inside the international lanes would kill it outright.

speculation.obs: Flight tracking put NATO maritime patrol aircraft off Russia's Kola bases the same week as the Svalbard seizure. As reported by Aftenposten, citing Flightradar24 and military officials, a British P-8 Poseidon departed Norway's Evenes air base and further NATO aircraft flew from Orland - home of Norway's F-35s - and from Bodo, running up the Norwegian coast and around Finnmark before circling in international airspace directly off Russia's naval bases on the Kola Peninsula. The newspaper's framing is that patrols of this kind have not been flown there for many years.
speculation.src: Aftenposten, citing Flightradar24 and military sources, relayed by News in English (Norway)
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and the species is a SIGNALLING FLIGHT - an observation made possible only because the aircraft chose to be trackable. Nothing about a P-8 off Kola is unusual as a mission; what is unusual is doing it in the open, from three Norwegian bases, in the days around a court-ordered arrest of a Russian state vessel at Barentsburg. The likeliest reading is deterrence messaging aimed at the Northern Fleet - a demonstration that the archipelago is watched - rather than preparation for anything. The competing boring explanation is real and should be held: routine ASW and NATO exercise cycles produce exactly this pattern, and one newspaper reading a flight tracker is not an order of battle.
speculation.falsifier: The flights stopping within a fortnight, or Norway confirming them as a pre-scheduled exercise, would mean this was calendar rather than signal. Continuation past the ship's release, or a matching Russian sortie pattern toward Svalbard, would confirm it.

speculation.obs: Tanker trackers have been logging Russia's Arctic workaround at latitudes with no commercial precedent. As reported by gCaptain using MagicPort Maritime Intelligence AIS data and Sentinel-1 satellite imagery, nearly twenty Suezmax, Aframax and Medium Range tankers were routed north of the Severnaya Zemlya archipelago above 81 degrees north in early August, after heavier ice persisted in the Vilkitsky Strait; roughly 8 million barrels were transiting or waiting to enter the Northern Sea Route, about 60 per cent of last season's 13.1 million barrel total, escorted by the nuclear icebreakers Sibir, Yakutiya and Ural. Named hulls include the Suezmax Dinasty and the Aframax Viktor Bakaev.
speculation.src: gCaptain, from MagicPort Maritime Intelligence AIS tracking and Sentinel-1 imagery
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and this is the physical backdrop that makes Svalbard something other than a shipping-news curiosity. Russia is building a crude export route that touches no chokepoint anyone else controls - not Hormuz, not Bab al-Mandab, not the Turkish straits - and pays for it in ice class, icebreaker time and insurance rather than in transit fees. That is the same substitutability logic as the diesel crack, run in reverse: Moscow is buying its way out of dependence on water it does not own. It also explains why an arrest at Barentsburg registers as more than symbolic in Moscow, and why South Korea has scheduled a September Busan-to-Rotterdam container trial on the same route, which requires Russian permitting to run at all.
speculation.falsifier: Northern Sea Route volumes finishing the season materially below last year's 13.1 million barrels, or the convoy reverting to Suez and Black Sea routings, would mean this is seasonal opportunism rather than a durable second rail. A completed non-Russian commercial transit under Russian permit would confirm the route is being institutionalised.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

Retaliation has gone HORIZONTAL: fire into US facilities in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in a single night widens the number of surfaces on which the interception equilibrium can fail, and converts Gulf hosts from venues into potential parties

The war has reached the LOADING POINT: Iranian state media says four US missiles hit a tanker six miles off Kharg on 5 September, and Iran fired anti-ship and ballistic missiles toward the strait the day before. Unconfirmed, and the terminals themselves are still unstruck - but the one asset with any convertible value left is now inside the target set

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

The covert front against the supplier coalition is now formally attributed: Berlin blames Moscow for an explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle and closes the Bonn consulate on Sept 18, with the EU calling it state-sponsored terrorism - salami tactics against logistics rather than against forces

First reciprocated pause of the war, and it is a bargaining instrument rather than fatigue: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight on 5 September, explicitly tied to the American envoys' visit, hours after striking Ukrainian airports and infrastructure and with Ryabkov restating that Washington must accept realities on the ground

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision for the next seven weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint, and it is a calendar rather than a character: a prime minister facing an election needs deliverables that are visible, mapped and finished, which is exactly what a declared security zone is. On 4 September Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge completes the phase of securing control in southern Lebanon and that there will be no withdrawal until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet, which makes the presence open-ended by construction. The desk that decides is not the cabinet podium but Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground costs manpower in a way air power does not. Note also the direction this cuts: history says a held buffer produces chronic attrition rather than episodic campaigns, which is why this board CUT its multi-week-campaign odds on the day the zone was declared. Separately, national security minister Ben Gvir published a twenty-page plan for what he calls voluntary emigration of Gaza's population - 250,000 in the first year and the remainder over six more. It is a minister's document rather than cabinet policy, and forced transfer of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; it is logged here as a coalition signal, not as a programme.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive at exactly the wrong moment
A withdrawal condition the Lebanese state cannot satisfy converts an operation into an occupation by definition
The Lebanon framework still has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Ministerial transfer plans for Gaza, even unimplemented, carry legal and coalition exposure that outlasts the cabinet

dossiers.name: Germany

glance.government: Federal parliamentary republic; coalition government under a chancellor with weak approval numbers
glance.leader: Friedrich Merz, chancellor; Alexander Dobrindt at the Interior Ministry carries the attribution and the police file, which is why the response is expulsions rather than an alliance consultation
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.9tn nominal - unverified against a current print; the binding number this quarter is energy input cost rather than headline output
glance.military: About 182,000 active on standard counts, with a rearmament programme running against recruitment shortfalls; unverified against a current IISS figure
glance.influence: Europe's largest industrial gas consumer, the logistics bridge to Ukraine through Leipzig/Halle, and the swing vote on every EU sanctions and energy instrument

dossiers.summary: Germany's constraint is a vice with an energy jaw and a security jaw, and both tightened this week. It replaced Russian pipeline gas with seaborne LNG, which traded a political dependency for a maritime one - so a war at Hormuz now reaches German industry directly, with continental storage near 62 percent against a seasonal norm around 79. At the same time it is the physical bridge over which munitions reach Ukraine, which is precisely why an explosive drone came down at Leipzig/Halle rather than at a barracks. Read the response for what it reveals about the ceiling: the desk that acted was the Interior Ministry, and the instruments were a consulate closure, a cultural-institute contract and visa tightening - the diplomatic rail, chosen because it is cheap, reversible and does not require asking twenty-six other governments for permission. The official story is resolve; the incentive read is a chancellor with poor ratings who gains from a clear adversary, which is a reason to scrutinise the timing rather than to assume it.

concerns: Gas storage near 62 percent with winter arriving is an industrial-cost problem before it is a household one, and German industry is the marginal European buyer
A sabotage campaign aimed at logistics rather than forces sits deliberately below any alliance threshold - which is what makes it repeatable
The attribution was published without forensics or charges, so its political durability depends on evidence Berlin has not yet shown
Moscow has promised to mirror the expulsions, which costs Germany intelligence access it may value more than the consulate it closed

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Pete Hegseth at Defense, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; federal debt past $40tn
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: The American constraint hardened today and it is arithmetic rather than politics. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, which removes the soft-landing argument for cutting; simultaneously diesel set an all-time record at $5.820 a gallon on a refining shortage no interest rate can fix. That is the RESCUE WITHHELD configuration - a market pricing help in a shock where help does not exist - and the long end already agrees, with the ten-year at 4.79% and the thirty-year at 5.27%, both above this board's published red lines, and the reverse-repo buffer down to $0.70bn. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the FOMC, the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, in that order of who can actually change the number. Foreign policy is being run on the same logic - allies invoiced for contributions at Hormuz, a Venezuelan venture organised around one man's legal exposure rather than around built infrastructure, and a president who declined this week to say whether the United States would defend Britain in another Falklands war. Each of those is leverage bought cheaply now against a commitment payable later.

concerns: Record diesel is the invisible half of the inflation problem, because it prices freight, farming and heating rather than only the pump
A hot labour print into a hiking debate removes the monetary rescue markets keep assuming
Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
Alliance ambiguity is being used as leverage in three theatres at once, and credibility spent in one is not recoverable in another
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

dossiers.name: Japan

glance.government: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; Bank of Japan policy decision due 18 September 2026
glance.leader: Emperor Naruhito as head of state; the Bank of Japan governorship is the office that matters for this file - the policy board, not the cabinet, sets the variable the world is watching
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.2tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; policy rate 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, with ten-year government bond yields near 3 per cent for the first time since 1996
glance.military: Self-Defense Forces of about 247,000 active personnel; defence spending on a path toward 2 per cent of GDP
glance.influence: The world's cheap funding currency, one of the largest foreign holders of US Treasuries, and a carry trade estimated anywhere between $500bn and over $4tn depending on definition

dossiers.summary: Japan appears on this board for a plumbing reason rather than a diplomatic one, and it is the reason the board opened a new forecast today. For thirty years Japan supplied the world with money that cost nothing - zero rates from 1999, then quantitative and qualitative easing from 2013 - and the world spent it on everything from Mexican bonds to American technology. That arrangement is now unwinding, not because Tokyo chose a new geopolitics but because Japan finally has inflation, imported partly through a weak yen and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption has made worse. The constraint on the policy board is therefore domestic and blunt: households are angry about food and fuel prices, exporters and the equity index need the weak currency, and every previous attempt to tighten has met that second constituency and delivered less than markets priced. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board on 18 September; the desk that transmits is the leveraged fund complex and the Japanese insurers and pension funds holding vast foreign bond portfolios. Watch the yen rather than the statement - a hike with the currency through 150 is the confirmation leg, and a hike with the yen drifting back above 160 is another false start in a long series.

concerns: A disorderly carry unwind transmits a Tokyo rate decision into global asset prices within hours, as it did in August 2024
The size of the borrowed-yen stack is genuinely unknown - published estimates span an order of magnitude
Higher domestic yields give Japanese institutions a reason to repatriate from Treasuries exactly as US issuance runs heaviest
Imported energy costs are the transmission line from the Strait of Hormuz into Japanese inflation and therefore into this policy decision

scenarios.q: What if the 72-hour Kyiv pause becomes an actual ceasefire?
scenarios.read: The mechanism is Reiter's expectation-convergence, and what matters is sequence rather than warmth. Wars end when both sides' estimates of the future converge, and a pause is how you test whether they have without paying for it. What makes this one different from the 2025 Easter truce is that it is reciprocated and dated on both sides at once. What makes it ordinary is everything else: no demarcation line, no monitoring, no guarantor, one city, three days, and a Russian deputy foreign minister restating maximalist terms on the same afternoon.

stages.s: Within 7 days: the pause is extended past 8 September or widened beyond Kyiv. Falsifier: it lapses on schedule with no extension, which sends GEO-005 back to 17 and is scored as a miss rather than deferred.
Within 60 days: a jointly acknowledged ceasefire-in-place text naming a demarcation line, even unsigned. Falsifier: sixty days of shuttle with no text either delegation will describe in public.
Within 6 months: a formal ceasefire holding more than 30 days - what GEO-005 resolves on at 20 per cent. Falsifier: a resumed general air campaign on the capital.
Beyond: an armistice with a monitored line and no treaty, which GEO-015 puts at 85 per cent conditional on the fighting stopping at all. Most branches die at stage A.

scenarios.falsifier: The pause lapsing on 8 September with no extension and no text kills this branch and scores today's raise a miss rather than deferring it.

scenarios.q: What if the Iran exchange breaks its interception equilibrium?
scenarios.read: Six months of exchanges have produced no American death and no struck US hull, and that is arithmetic rather than restraint - target-matched volleys, high interception rates, and two governments that each get to claim a result. What changed this weekend is the SURFACE: Iranian anti-ship and ballistic launches toward the strait on Friday, and a reported American strike on a commercial hull at Iran's loading anchorage on Saturday. Equilibria of this kind fail at their widest edge, and the edge just moved from military targets to shipping.

stages.s: Within 14 days: a second strike on shipping in the northern Gulf loading zone, or a confirmed hit on a laden tanker inside the international lanes. Falsifier: a fortnight of quiet, or Muscat publishing corridor coordinates.

Within 30 days: a confirmed American death or a struck US-flagged hull - the published CRITICAL trigger on this board. Falsifier: the trigger unfired on 5 October, logged as scored rather than deferred.
Within 60 days of such an event: a sustained multi-week campaign against Iranian state targets, which is GEO-003 at 46 per cent.
Beyond: a strike on Kharg's loading terminals themselves, ending Iranian seaborne export rather than taxing it. Most branches die at stage A, which is why the terminals are wired separately.

scenarios.falsifier: Fourteen days with no further attack on shipping plus a published minesweeping calendar out of Muscat kills this branch, sends GEO-003 back toward 38 and GEO-001 back toward 21 - scored as a miss, not deferred.

scenarios.q: What if Germany's firewall holds and the state becomes ungovernable?
scenarios.read: The mechanism is arithmetic, not sentiment. A cordon sanitaire denies partners; it does nothing to a party that reaches a majority alone, and it costs the excluding bloc its own options. The CDU in Saxony-Anhalt has ruled out both the AfD and Die Linke and polls around 22 per cent, which means the interesting failure mode is not a far-right government - it is no government at all, and a second election fought on the question of who made the state ungovernable.

stages.s: Sunday night: the AfD takes the most seats but falls short of an absolute majority. Falsifier: an outright seat majority, which resolves GEO-028 almost immediately and kills this branch by the other door.

Within 90 days: a CDU-led minority government, or a CDU arrangement with Die Linke that breaks a second taboo in order to preserve the first. Falsifier: a stable conventional coalition seated without either.
Within 18 months: repeat elections in the Land, or an AfD Minister-President anywhere in Germany - GEO-028 at 16 per cent. Falsifier: a government seated and surviving a budget vote.
Beyond: the federal CDU formally softens the Brandmauer at Land level. Most branches die at stage A or B and this one is designed to.

scenarios.falsifier: A conventional coalition seated in Magdeburg within 90 days kills this branch outright and scores the ungovernability read a miss.

scenarios.q: What if the diesel squeeze outlasts the war that caused it?
scenarios.read: The mechanism is capital stock, not conflict. Crude supply responds to price in weeks because valves open; refining supply responds in years because units get built, and nobody builds a hydrocracker on a two-year price signal in a decarbonising policy environment. So the question is not whether the shooting stops - it is whether, when it does, the world discovers it had been running on refining slack that no longer exists. Three pulls are live at once: Gulf product flows through a contested strait, Russian refineries under drone attack with an export ban to 30 September, and Western turnaround intervals stretched past prudence. Only one of the three has a published expiry date.

stages.s: Within 30 days: the crack stays above $70 and at least one government moves from complaint to allocation - an export restriction floated, a distillate reserve release, a farm-diesel subsidy. Falsifier: the crack settles under $45 and this branch dies here, which is exactly what GEO-026 is written to score.

Within 90 days: heating-season demand meets record-low East Coast stocks and diesel becomes an explicitly political price in the US midterm campaign, the way petrol was in 2022. Falsifier: East Coast distillate rebuilding above 30 million barrels before 1 December.

Within 6 months: refining margin becomes a stated object of policy - windfall levies, domestic supply obligations, or a state-backed refinery programme in a G7 country. Falsifier: no G7 legislature tables a refining-specific measure.

Beyond: the least substitutable step in the oil chain sits permanently outside the West - Jamnagar, Ruwais, Dangote and Chinese teapots setting the world diesel price the way Rotterdam once did. Most branches die at stage A or B.

scenarios.falsifier: A US diesel crack settling below $45 a barrel before 15 December with the strait still contested kills this branch outright and scores the outage read - published as a miss rather than as not yet.

easy.bottomLine: Two very different things happened today and both matter. In the Gulf, Iranian state TV says American missiles hit an Iranian oil tanker near Kharg Island - the place where Iran actually loads its oil onto ships. Nobody has confirmed it except Iran, so treat it carefully. But if it is true, it crosses a line both sides had quietly kept for six months: hitting ships and the loading area, not just soldiers and weapons. Meanwhile in Moscow, two American envoys landed with a plan to end the war in Ukraine, and Russia promised not to bomb Kyiv for three days while they visit. Ukraine promised to stop its own air attacks too. That is the first time in this entire war that both sides have promised to stop something at the same time - which is genuinely new, even though it is only three days and only one city.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, and not higher, because of a rule we wrote down in advance: it only goes to the top step if an American is killed in a new attack or an American-flagged ship is hit. Neither happened. We also gave ourselves a specific test about attacks on tankers in the shipping lanes of the Strait of Hormuz - and today's reported attack was not in the shipping lanes, it was 250 miles up the coast where oil gets loaded. We are not going to bend our own test to make today's news fit it. One thing pointed the other way, too: a credit rating agency, whose entire job is to worry, decided Qatar's gas plants are less likely to be blown up than it thought back in March.
easy.markets: Oil finished the week around $96 a barrel, up almost 9 per cent - and then the tanker news broke on Saturday, with markets closed. That is the thing to hold in your head: an important piece of news arrived when nobody could trade on it, so Monday morning is a guess rather than a price. Separately, the US government still cannot borrow cheaply. The interest rate on its long-term debt sits right at the level we flag as a warning line, which matters because when a government's borrowing gets expensive, everyone else's eventually does too.
brief: Iranian state television says four American missiles hit an oil tanker near Kharg Island, where Iran loads most of its oil onto ships. Nobody was hurt, and no government has confirmed it. If it is true, it is the first time this war has moved from hitting soldiers and weapons to hitting the ships themselves.

Two American envoys flew to Moscow with a plan to end the war in Ukraine, and Russia agreed not to bomb Kyiv for three days while they are there. Ukraine agreed to stop its air attacks too. It is only three days and only one city - but it is the first time in this war that both sides promised to stop at the same time.

Germany votes tomorrow in one of its states, and a far-right party is polling above 40 per cent, far ahead of everyone else. All the other parties refuse to govern with it - but that refusal only works if the party needs a partner. If it wins enough seats to rule on its own, the refusal stops mattering.

America's Defence Department has taken a 35 per cent share of a Venezuelan oil company. Reuters reports the businessman running it was being investigated for laundering money stolen from Venezuela's state oil company - and that US prosecutors were discouraged from pursuing it while officials worked to get the deal done.

The US ambassador to Israel visited a Palestinian town that keeps being attacked by settlers, and called the attackers terrorists. That is surprising because he has spent his career on the settlers' side of the argument. The town has American citizens living in it, which is probably the real reason he went.

risk.line: Still HIGH, and the reason to say it out loud today is that the tape got hotter without touching our published trigger. The top step requires a confirmed American death in a new incident or a struck US-flagged hull, and neither happened. What happened instead is that Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting says four American missiles hit an Iranian oil tanker about six miles off Kharg Island on Saturday morning, crew evacuating, no casualties reported. Hold that at arm's length: it is single-sourced to the party it benefits, CENTCOM did not respond, no Iranian official has commented and no evidence has been published. If it is true it is a first of its class - American ordnance on a commercial hull at Iran's principal loading anchorage rather than on Iranian military assets - and there is a rung on the ladder that was empty yesterday. It follows Iranian anti-ship and ballistic launches from Isfahan and Kerman toward the strait on Friday. Two counterweights belong in the same paragraph rather than in a footnote. First, our own published Hormuz falsifier is NOT fired and is not being quietly reinterpreted to fit the news: it requires an attack on a laden tanker inside the INTERNATIONAL LANES, and Kharg is a loading anchorage roughly 250 nautical miles up the Gulf; seventeen days left to run. Second, a professional desk marked the destruction risk DOWN today - Fitch removed Qatar from Rating Watch Negative citing reduced risk to its LNG facilities since March while keeping the negative outlook for the blockade, which is a ratings committee separating the risk that the plant is destroyed from the risk that the cargo cannot leave. On the other board, the first genuinely two-sided move of this war: Putin instructed that no strikes be carried out on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight, Zelenskyy said Ukraine would halt its own airstrikes, and Witkoff and Kushner landed in Moscow with a Kyiv leg on Sunday. And the financial red board eased to YELLOW, which we score as carefully as we would score an alarm.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: RAISED 3, and the reason this is a raise rather than a fourth repetition of one read is that the OBSERVABLE CHANGED CLASS. For three sessions this book moved on the channel-is-alive read - a reported trip, a Putin remark, a TASS single source - and the 30 August audit was right to flag it. Today the trip happened, confirmed by Reuters, the BBC and Russian state media, and something new sits on top of it: a reciprocated, dated cessation. Peskov said Putin instructed that no strikes be carried out on Kyiv for three days from midnight Saturday, explicitly connected to the preparation and conduct of the American contacts in Kyiv; Zelenskyy said Ukraine would halt its own airstrikes for the visit. That is the first two-sided dated pause of this war. Reiter is the anchor - wars end when belligerents' expectations converge, and a mutual observed pause is the cheapest costly signal available to test whether they have. Capped at 3 and held far below the mood for three reasons kept in front: Ryabkov said Washington must account for realities on the ground where the situation is changing not in Kyiv's favour, which is the maximalist position restated; Russia struck Ukrainian airports and infrastructure hours before the pause with at least five killed; and the base rate on short visit-linked pauses converting into 30-day-plus ceasefires is poor, with the 2025 Easter truce and the energy-infrastructure moratorium as the local precedents and both lapsed. Fortna is why it stays at 20 - durable ceasefires have monitoring, demarcation and guarantors, and this has none. NEW DATED FALSIFIER, replacing the 14 September envoy window which resolved today on the confirming side: if the pause lapses on 8 September with no extension and no jointly acknowledged text, this comes straight back to 17.

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: RAISED 3 on three distinct escalation legs inside 48 hours, and capped at 3 by a professional desk marking the risk the other way. The legs: Iran launched anti-ship and ballistic missiles from Isfahan and Kerman toward the strait on Friday, apparently at maritime activity; Iranian state broadcasting says four American missiles hit a tanker about six miles off Kharg on Saturday; and Trump said the US may hit Pickaxe Mountain very soon, adding that Washington knows everybody that is moving there. The framework is recurrence hazard, and it is the same read that governs GEO-001 - which is exactly why GEO-001 is NOT moved today. These facts speak to campaign tempo, not to transit volume, and spending one fact on two questions is the double-count the 30 August audit named. The counterweight is published rather than buried: Fitch removed Qatar from Rating Watch Negative today citing reduced risk to its LNG facilities since March, while keeping the negative outlook for the blockade. A ratings committee paid to be pessimistic has separated the risk of destruction from the risk of non-delivery and marked the first one down. That is real evidence against a broad new campaign on Gulf energy infrastructure, and it is why this is 46 rather than 50.

forecasts.q: Brent stays inside the $80-100 band
forecasts.note: CUT 4 on geometry and variance rather than on a print - and it must be said plainly that there IS no print, because today is Saturday and the escalation arrived with the market shut. Brent settled around $96 on Friday, up nearly 9 per cent on the week and roughly four per cent under the barrier. Into that closed market went a reported American strike on a commercial hull at Iran's principal loading anchorage. First-passage probability - the chance a price TOUCHES a level before a deadline - is a function of distance, time and volatility, and it is the third term that moved: an unpriced weekend escalation raises the variance of Monday's open without changing the distance. Nineteen days remain and the $80 floor is effectively dead while the strait is contested, so nearly all the risk to this question sits on one side. The wording is restated for the fourth session because it decides the score: this resolves on DAILY CLOSES, and the $99.38 of 2 September was an INTRADAY print, so nothing has breached. Still the closest call on the board and our first Brier score, on 24 September.

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to US happens in September
forecasts.note: RAISED 2 on sunk organisational cost, which is the only kind of evidence a scheduled-visit question should move on. Reuters reports Xi assembling an unusually large CEO delegation for the 24 September summit - unusual because Beijing has spent years keeping private enterprise off the diplomatic stage and because American scrutiny of Chinese investment makes it a risk; Notus separately reports a state dinner in preparation. Neither is a statement of intent, and that is the point - a delegation is a manifest and a state dinner is a guest list, and a party planning to cancel pays for neither. Nineteen days out with no public dispute. The same fact would also argue for cutting GEO-007, and GEO-007 is deliberately HELD: one fact, one question.

forecasts.q: NEW - An AfD politician is sworn in as Minister-President of a German Land before 31 Dec 2027
forecasts.note: OPENED at 16, paying a European domestic-politics coverage debt on the eve of the vote that creates it - and opened BEFORE the result, so it is scoreable rather than retrospective. Saxony-Anhalt votes on 6 September with the AfD polling about 41.8 per cent against the CDU's 22.4, Die Linke 12.3, SPD 7.6, Greens 5.4, BSW 3.9 and FDP 3.2. The base rate is the anchor and it is absolute: no far-right party has led a German Land since 1945, and the Brandmauer has held through every previous surge including Thuringia in 2024, where the AfD won the most votes at 32.8 per cent and was still excluded. The reason this is 16 and not 5 is arithmetic rather than mood - a firewall is a COALITION instrument and it is irrelevant against an absolute majority of SEATS, which 41.8 per cent of votes can produce when small parties miss the five per cent threshold. On the current numbers that path exists but does not close: even with BSW, the FDP and the Greens all excluded, the AfD lands near 48 per cent of seats, so it needs a polling beat as well as threshold waste, and eastern polls have historically understated the AfD only modestly. The second-order case is the one nobody prices - if the AfD falls short, a CDU that has ruled out both the AfD and Die Linke commands about a third of the chamber and the state becomes very hard to govern at all. Resolution is a document: a sworn-in Minister-President, not a poll and not a coalition rumour.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover past 50% of pre-war volume
forecasts.note: HELD, and this is the most deliberate non-move of the day. The facts are transit-negative - anti-ship launches into the strait on Friday, a reported strike on a tanker at Kharg on Saturday, 87 vessels redirected since the campaign opened - but they are the SAME facts that bought GEO-003 three points, and this question resolves on VOLUME rather than on tempo. One point matters more than the number: our published cluster falsifier is NOT fired and is not being reinterpreted to make today's news fit it. It requires an attack on a laden tanker inside the INTERNATIONAL LANES; Kharg is a loading anchorage roughly 250 nautical miles up the Gulf from the strait. Seventeen days left to run, and a reopening to half of pre-war volume remains a minesweeping and insurance problem before it is a diplomatic one.

forecasts.q: US commits to fixed Venezuelan heavy-crude export infrastructure
forecasts.note: HELD at 36, three days from its own test, and the hold IS the discipline. Today's Reuters investigation adds real detail - Florida prosecutors paused the money-laundering inquiry into the venture's operator, supervisors discouraged pursuing it, US officials pressed Bern until Switzerland dropped its extradition request in May, and Spain has opened a separate inquiry into $4bn - but that is the same argument this book already spent three points on yesterday. Repeating an argument is not new evidence. The 8 September signing session is the test: a published instrument with a governing law, an arbitration seat and a named sanctions authorisation moves this. Another briefing does not.

forecasts.q: US-China tariff truce collapses before Nov expiry
forecasts.note: HELD, and explicitly so. The CEO-delegation and state-dinner reporting that bought GEO-006 two points argues in the same direction here, and moving both would be spending one fact twice - the exact error the audit named. The live observable is unchanged: whether the 7.5 per cent overcapacity layer is published and imposed before 24 September, or quietly delayed past the summit.

forecasts.q: Fed's standing T-bill purchase program still running at end-2026
forecasts.note: HELD at 93 for the fifth day. Overnight reverse repo printed $0.68bn, down 53 per cent on the month, so the reserve-adequacy case for the bill programme is if anything stronger - and that is precisely why it does not move. This is a standing prior, and re-marking it upward on the continuation of its own evidence is how a 93 becomes an unfalsifiable 99.

forecasts.q: US Hormuz concession within 30 days after the Xi summit
forecasts.note: HELD, and the hold is argued because today's evidence cuts both ways. A government that strikes a tanker and threatens a nuclear site three weeks before a summit does not look like one assembling a concession package - but escalate-then-settle is the oldest sequence in coercive bargaining, and Schelling would read today's tempo as bargaining rather than as war. Genuinely ambiguous evidence is a reason not to move, not a reason to pick the more interesting side. What moves this is a concession-shaped artefact: an unfreeze tranche, a waiver, or accepted Iranian route-coordination.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
